title: Harmonize rate-limit headers and keyed idempotency in OpenAI-compat adapter
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Standardize OpenAI-compat rate-limit headers and idempotency semantics: SDKs and integrators should rely on X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After canonicalization. Add new consistent error codes for rate_limit and idempotency_failure. Rollout behind feature flag; no customer action required for most deployments.
description:
Context: The OpenAI-compat adapter has historically normalized vendor rate-limit headers in multiple ad-hoc places which led to inconsistent Retry-After handling across streaming and non-streaming endpoints and unreliable idempotency deduplication when requests were retried across internal proxies.
This PR centralizes header parsing and idempotency lifecycle handling in the compat adapter so downstream code (streaming, function/tool-calls, structured-output) can rely on a single set of semantics.
Motivation: Fix two production classes of issues we see in SLO alerts and incident postmortems: 1) streaming connections being closed prematurely when transient rate-limit headers were present but contained non-standard values (e.g. float seconds, comma lists, or vendor-specific names); 2) duplicate side-effects when idempotency keys were not deduplicated consistently across retries and replayed through the fallback routing layer.
Changes in this PR:
- Add a single RateLimitParser that canonicalizes common header shapes (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After, Retry-After-Milliseconds) and returns a deterministic object to the adapter. Parser implements tolerant parsing for floats, comma-separated values (takes first valid), and RFC 7231 date parsing.
- Introduce keyed idempotency policy in compat adapter: idempotency keys are normalized, hashed (SHA256 prefix), and stored in the internal dedupe cache with a configurable TTL that varies by route (default 60s for generation endpoints, 300s for tooling calls). The policy includes 'last-result' metadata to support deterministic replay for clients expecting the same completion when retrying.
- Streaming behavior: adaptors now surface rate-limit signals to the streaming mux layer instead of unilaterally closing streams. When a transient rate-limit is detected and the request is eligible for retry/fallback, the stream is paused and an idempotent retry is attempted (server-initiated), otherwise the stream sends a structured error event with our new error code "rate_limit" and a recommended "retry_after_ms" integer field.
- Error schema: add stable OpenAI-compat error codes: rate_limit, idempotency_failure, transient_backend_error. Each error includes message, type, code, and optionally retry_after_ms. This unifies behaviour across CLI/SDK and avoids ambiguous HTTP 429 handling.
- Backwards compatibility: old headers are still accepted, feature gated behind compat.features.new_rate_handling (default true for canary). Old adapter behavior is preserved when the flag is off.
- Tests: extensive unit tests for header permutations, idempotency TTL expiry, and streaming integration tests that simulate partial Retry-After formats and brokered fallback.
- Observability: add new metrics: compat.rate_limit_parsed.errors, compat.idempotency.hits, compat.idempotency.misses, compat.rate_limit.retry_attempts.
- Docs: update openai-compat README with the canonical header list and an SDK migration note.
Commits summary:
- 1a2b3c4: add RateLimitParser and unit tests
- 2b3c4d5: implement idempotency cache interface and TTL config
- 3c4d5e6: wire parser into adapter request path and expose canonical fields to stream mux
- 4d5e6f7: streaming integration tests and structured error payloads
- 5e6f7g8: docs and feature flag rollout config
Files changed (high level):
- src/openai_compat/adapter.py: central header parsing and idempotency orchestration (key logic)
- src/openai_compat/ratelimit.py: new tolerant parser and helpers
- src/openai_compat/idempotency.py: cache interface + hashing helpers
- src/openai_compat/stream_mux.py: pause/resume hooks and structured error emission
- tests/unit/test_ratelimit.py, tests/integration/test_streaming_rate_limit.py
- docs/openai_compat.md
Notes on behavior and edge cases:
- Retry-After parsing: we prefer numeric seconds when present, but support HTTP-date format; in ambiguous cases we return retry_after_ms=null to signal SDKs should apply client-side backoff heuristics.
- Comma lists are common in some vendors; parser will pick the first parsable token (documented).
- Idempotency collision risk is mitigated by storing a 16-byte prefix of SHA256 and the full last-result checksum; we log collisions at debug level and surface idempotency_failure when conflicting non-idempotent results are detected.
Rollout plan:
- Canary 5% on dedicated infra with feature flag enabled for 72h and close monitoring on new metrics.
- Expand to 50% if no elevated rate_limit_parsed.errors or idempotency_failure spikes.
- Full rollout targeted in next stable release after monitoring window.
Migration guidance for integrators:
- SDKs should prefer inspecting error.code rather than HTTP status for retry decisions.
- If you rely on custom Retry-After parsing, switch to the canonical fields once SDKs consume them.
- For deterministic replay across retries, include an idempotency key on generation and tooling endpoints; keys should be stable across retries.
Testing notes and CI:
- CI had an initial flaky test in streaming harness (mock timeouts) which was fixed by adding deterministic fake-clock in tests, see commit 4d5e6f7.
- All builds green on final run.
Related work: ENG-5123 (rate-limit standardization), ENG-5187 (idempotency cache interface), SUP-1247 (customer report about duplicate charge issue).
